subject: math
title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions
seo_title: Grade 6 Adding and Subtracting Fractions Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Use tools to add and subtract fractions, including fractions with unlike denominators, in various contexts
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on adding and subtracting fractions for the Ontario curriculum: like, related and unlike denominators, fraction bars, number lines, mixed numbers with regrouping and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, great for EQAO practice.
key_big: Add or subtract fractions only when the parts are the same size: use a common denominator, then add or subtract the numerators.
key_sub: 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8 (keep the denominator). 1/3 + 1/4 = 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12, not 2/7. With mixed numbers, regroup 1 whole when the first fraction is smaller.
body_html:
Same denominator: add the numerators

The denominator tells the size of the parts. The numerator tells how many parts. When the denominators are the same, add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator.

Example

710 − 310 = ?

Subtract the numerators: 7 − 3 = 4. Keep tenths: 410. Simplify: divide both by 2.

Answer: 25

Different denominators: make the parts the same size

Thirds and fourths are different sizes, so first find a common denominator: a number that both denominators divide into. Then write each fraction as an equivalent fraction with that denominator.

Example

13 + 14 = ?

Common denominator: 12. 13 = 412 and 14 = 312. Add the numerators: 4 + 3 = 7.

Answer: 712

On a number line split into twelfths, start at 13 (4 steps) and jump forward 14 (3 steps). You land on 712.

Find the common denominator

If one denominator is a multiple of the other (related denominators), use the bigger one. Otherwise, find the lowest common multiple of the two denominators. Multiplying the denominators always works too, but the numbers get bigger.

FractionsCommon denominatorEquivalent fractions
12 and 38848 and 38
23 and 1412812 and 312
56 and 34121012 and 912

Give answers in simplest form. If the answer is an improper fraction, write it as a mixed number.

Example

56 + 34 = ?

1012 + 912 = 1912. 19 ÷ 12 = 1 remainder 7, so 1912 = 1 712.

Answer: 1 712

Mixed numbers and regrouping

Write the fraction parts with a common denominator. Then add or subtract the fractions and the whole numbers.

CalculationEquivalent fractionsFractionsWhole numbersAnswer
2 13 + 1 142 412 + 1 3127122 + 1 = 33 712
2 23 + 1 342 812 + 1 9121712 = 1 5122 + 1 + 1 = 44 512
3 14 − 1 233 312 − 1 812regroup: 2 15122 − 1 = 11 712

In the last row, 312 is less than 812, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 1212. 3 312 = 2 1512.

Example

3 14 − 1 23 = ?

3 312 − 1 812. Regroup: 3 312 = 2 1512. Fractions: 1512 − 812 = 712. Whole numbers: 2 − 1 = 1.

Answer: 1 712

Another way: change both to improper fractions. 3 14 = 3912 and 1 23 = 2012. 3912 − 2012 = 1912 = 1 712.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
38 + 28 = 516 (adding the denominators)Keep the denominator: 3 eighths + 2 eighths = 58
13 + 14 = 27 (adding the numerators and the denominators)Use a common denominator: 412 + 312 = 712
12 + 38 = 48 (changing the denominator but not the numerator)Multiply the numerator by the same number: 12 = 48, so the total is 78
3 14 − 1 23 = 2 512 (taking 312 from 812)Regroup 1 whole: 2 1512 − 1 812 = 1 712
2 23 + 1 34 = 3 1712 (not regrouping)Change 1712 to 1 512 and add it to the wholes: 4 512

faq.q: What does the Ontario Grade 6 math curriculum say about adding and subtracting fractions?
faq.a: In strand B (Number), Grade 6 students use tools to add and subtract fractions, including fractions with unlike denominators, in various contexts. Fraction bars, number lines and common denominators are all good tools.

faq.q: How do you add fractions with different denominators?
faq.a: Find a common denominator, write both fractions as equivalent fractions with it, then add the numerators. For 1/3 + 1/4, use twelfths: 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12.

faq.q: How do you subtract mixed numbers when you need to regroup?
faq.a: If the first fraction is smaller, rename 1 whole as a fraction. For 3 1/4 − 1 2/3, write 3 3/12 − 1 8/12, regroup to 2 15/12 − 1 8/12, and the answer is 1 7/12.

faq.q: Are fractions on the Grade 6 EQAO math test?
faq.a: The Grade 6 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario curriculum expectations, and Number, including fractions, is a big part of it. Practising with fraction models and word problems is good preparation.

items.e: The lowest common multiple of 5 and 2 is 10, so use 10 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 6 25 = 6 410 and 3 12 = 3 510. 410 is less than 510, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 1010. 6 410 = 5 1410. Subtract the fractions: 1410 − 510 = 910. Subtract the whole numbers: 5 − 3 = 2. The answer is 2 910.

items.q:
7 18 − 4 34 = ?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 4, so use 8 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 4 34 = 4 68. 18 is less than 68, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 88. 7 18 = 6 98. Subtract the fractions: 98 − 68 = 38. Subtract the whole numbers: 6 − 4 = 2. The answer is 2 38.

items.q:
4 − 1 23 = ?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: There is no fraction to take 23 from, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 33. 4 = 3 33. Subtract the fractions: 33 − 23 = 13. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 1 = 2. The answer is 2 13.

items.q:
Mei is making pancakes for a weekend breakfast. The recipe uses 34 cup of milk and 13 cup of water. How much liquid is that altogether?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 3 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 34 = 912 and 13 = 412. Add the numerators: 912 + 412 = 1312. 1312 is an improper fraction: 1312 = 1 112. The answer is 1 112 cups.

items.q:
A 2 L jug of lemonade is full. At the class picnic, Priya pours 34 L into cups and Leah pours 23 L. How much lemonade is left in the jug?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: First add what they pour. Use twelfths: 912 + 812 = 1712 = 1 512 L. Then 2 − 1 512: regroup 1 whole, 2 = 1 1212. 1 1212 − 1 512 = 712 L.

items.q:
Amira practises piano for 23 of an hour on Monday and 14 of an hour on Tuesday. How long does she practise altogether?
Give your answer in simplest form.
c: 37 of an hour
34 of an hour
14 of an hour
1112 of an hour
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 23 = 812 and 14 = 312. Add the numerators: 812 + 312 = 1112. The answer is 1112 of an hour. (That is 55 minutes.)

items.q:
Olivia plans to practise guitar for 1 14 hours this week. She has practised for 23 of an hour so far. How much practice time is left?
Give your answer in simplest form.
c: 712 of an hour
512 of an hour
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 3 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 1 14 = 1 312 and 23 = 812. 312 is less than 812, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 1212. 1 312 = 1512. Subtract the fractions: 1512 − 812 = 712. The answer is 712 of an hour. (That is 35 minutes.)

items.q:
Chloe has 3 13 m of ribbon. She uses 1 34 m to decorate a Thanksgiving centrepiece. How much ribbon is left?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 3 13 = 3 412 and 1 34 = 1 912. 412 is less than 912, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 1212. 3 412 = 2 1612. Subtract the fractions: 1612 − 912 = 712. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 1 = 1. The answer is 1 712 m.

items.q:
In the school garden, 13 of the ground is for vegetables and 25 is for herbs. The rest is for flowers. What fraction of the garden is for flowers?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: First add the parts that are used. Use fifteenths: 13 = 515 and 25 = 615, so 515 + 615 = 1115. The whole garden is 1515. Flowers: 1515 − 1115 = 415.

items.q:
Emma eats 14 of a pizza and Sofia eats 13 of it. What fraction of the pizza is left?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: First add what they eat. Use twelfths: 312 + 412 = 712. The whole pizza is 1212. Left: 1212 − 712 = 512.

items.q:
On a canoe trip, a family paddles 2 14 km to an island and then 1 23 km to their campsite. How far do they paddle altogether?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 3 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 2 14 = 2 312 and 1 23 = 1 812. Add the fractions: 312 + 812 = 1112. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. The answer is 3 1112 km.

items.q:
At the Terry Fox Run, Ava runs 1 34 km. Jayden runs 1 56 km. How much farther does Jayden run than Ava?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: “How much farther” means subtract. The lowest common multiple of 6 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 1 56 = 1 1012 and 1 34 = 1 912. Subtract the fractions: 1012 − 912 = 112. Subtract the whole numbers: 1 − 1 = 0. The answer is 112 km.

items.q:
A jug holds 1 12 L of apple juice. Arjun pours 58 L into glasses. How much juice is left in the jug?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 2, so use 8 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 1 12 = 1 48. 48 is less than 58, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 88. 1 48 = 128. Subtract the fractions: 128 − 58 = 78. The answer is 78 L.

items.q:
A bread recipe needs 34 kg of flour. Liam has two open bags with 12 kg and 18 kg left in them. How much more flour does he need?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: He has 12 + 18 = 48 + 18 = 58 kg. He needs 34 = 68 kg. 68 − 58 = 18 kg more.

items.q:
A recipe for maple oatmeal cookies uses 1 14 cups of rolled oats and 56 cup of flour. How many cups is that altogether?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 1 14 = 1 312 and 56 = 1012. Add the fractions: 312 + 1012 = 1312. The whole number is 1. 1312 is an improper fraction: 1312 = 1 112. 1 + 1 112 = 2 112. The answer is 2 112 cups.

items.q:
A Saturday hockey tournament lasts 4 12 hours. The lunch break takes 34 of an hour. How much time is left for games?
Give your answer in simplest form.
c: 34 of an hour
items.e: 4 is a multiple of 2, so use 4 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 4 12 = 4 24. 24 is less than 34, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 44. 4 24 = 3 64. Subtract the fractions: 64 − 34 = 34. The whole number left is 3. The answer is 3 34 hours. (That is 3 hours 45 minutes.)

items.q:
Zoe has soccer practice for 1 13 hours on Tuesday and 1 12 hours on Thursday. How many hours of practice is that altogether?
Give your answer in simplest form.
c: 56 of an hour
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 2 is 6, so use 6 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 1 13 = 1 26 and 1 12 = 1 36. Add the fractions: 26 + 36 = 56. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 1 = 2. The answer is 2 56 hours. (That is 2 hours 50 minutes.)

items.q:
Two boards, 2 23 m and 1 45 m long, are joined end to end to edge a garden bed. What is the total length?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 5 is 15, so use 15 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 2 23 = 2 1015 and 1 45 = 1 1215. Add the fractions: 1015 + 1215 = 2215. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. 2215 is an improper fraction: 2215 = 1 715. 3 + 1 715 = 4 715. The answer is 4 715 m.

items.q:
In a Grade 6 class, 12 of the students walk to school and 13 take the school bus. The rest come by car. What fraction of the class comes by car?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: Add the two groups. Use sixths: 36 + 26 = 56. The whole class is 66. Driven by car: 66 − 56 = 16.

items.q:
Owen’s bike ride to the community centre is 1 16 km. He has ridden 34 km so far. How far is left to ride?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: Work out 1 16 − 34. Use twelfths: 1 16 = 1412 and 34 = 912. 1412 − 912 = 512 km. Check: 912 + 512 = 1412 = 1 16.

items.q: Noah spends 25 of an hour on math homework and 13 of an hour reading. He says that is 38 of an hour altogether. Which is true?
c: He is wrong. It is 15
He is wrong. It is 1115
He is wrong. It is 215
items.e: Noah added the numerators and the denominators. Use fifteenths: 615 + 515 = 1115. Also, 38 is less than 25, so it cannot be the total. The answer is 1115.

items.q: A pizza is cut into equal slices. Which two fractions of the pizza make the whole pizza?
c: 34 and 312
12 and 38
23 and 16
35 and 310
items.e: 34 = 912, and 912 + 312 = 1212 = 1, so 34 and 312 is correct. The other totals are 56, 910 and 78.

items.q:
For Thanksgiving dinner, a family buys 1 34 kg of potatoes and 2 13 kg of squash. How many kilograms of vegetables is that altogether?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 3 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 1 34 = 1 912 and 2 13 = 2 412. Add the fractions: 912 + 412 = 1312. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 2 = 3. 1312 is an improper fraction: 1312 = 1 112. 3 + 1 112 = 4 112. The answer is 4 112 kg.
